Soil and terrain at Green Mountain Park

Green Mountain Park is a mountain bike trail network in Denver & Golden, CO. Soil data at the sampled location is classified as rocky sandy. Open tree cover can allow more sun and wind exposure, helping drying. Terrain data indicates an elevation of about 6,792 ft, an average terrain slope of 7.3° and a predominant SW-facing aspect. Terrain slope does not measure the trail tread or its drainage features. Trails here include Summit Loop, North Access and Box O Rox Trail. Loam models conditions across the network; individual trails and constructed surfaces can differ from these environmental inputs. Official closures and conditions on the ground take priority.

How we check ourselves

How these factors affect drying

SoilRocky sandy

The soil data includes about 55% rock fragments. The model uses this to adjust drainage; it does not measure how quickly every trail section dries. Drying behavior is modeled from the soil classification, not measured directly on the trail.

CanopyOpen 14%

Open tree cover can allow more sunlight and wind to reach the ground. Terrain, weather and trail construction also affect drying.

TerrainSteep

Steeper terrain can encourage runoff. Terrain slope does not measure the trail tread or its drainage features.

What is the soil and trail surface like at Green Mountain Park?

How long does Green Mountain Park take to dry after rain?

Green Mountain Park has no fixed drying time. Rainfall, soil moisture, shade and the weather that follows all matter. The model accounts for about 55% rock fragments in the soil data, but that does not establish a recovery time. Check the current estimate and wait until the trail surface is firm.

Can you ride Green Mountain Park after rain?

Rock fragments influence the drying model, but softer trail sections may need more time. Wait until the surface is firm. Check the current estimate before heading out, and turn back if your tires leave ruts.

What does a frozen condition mean at Green Mountain Park?

FROZEN means Loam estimates snow cover or frozen ground. It does not establish that riding is allowed or that every trail is frozen. Check posted winter access rules and watch for soft ground as temperatures rise.

What trails are at Green Mountain Park?

Trails at Green Mountain Park include Green Mountain, Rooney Valley Trail, Summit Loop, North Access and Box O Rox Trail. This is a partial list. The condition estimate covers the whole network, so individual trails may differ.

What's the terrain and elevation like at Green Mountain Park?

Terrain data indicates an elevation of about 6,792 ft, an average terrain slope of 7.3° and a predominant SW-facing aspect. Terrain slope does not measure the trail tread or its drainage features.
